1k mouse heart cells, as a Seurat object

Source: R/data.R
heart1k.Rd

A cut-down copy of the 10x Genomics "1k Heart Cells from an E18 Mouse (v3 chemistry)" demo run, already read through seuratFrom10x() so examples can start from a Seurat object. The same data ships as a Cell Ranger outs/ directory for the path-based readers – see Bundled Cell Ranger output below.

Usage

heart1k

Format

A SeuratObject::Seurat object: 2,092 genes x 1,011 cells, one RNA assay of raw counts, with orig.ident and Ident both "heart_1k_v3". Rows are mouse gene symbols.

Source

10x Genomics, Cell Ranger 3.0.0, mm10 reference: https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/1-k-heart-cells-from-an-e-18-mouse-v-3-chemistry-3-standard-3-0-0. The full FASTQs (6.4 GB) are downloadable from the same page. The script that builds this subset is data-raw/heart_1k_v3.R in the package source.

Details

Every cell Cell Ranger called is kept, but only 2,092 of the 31,053 genes: the 2,000 detected in the most cells, plus every mitochondrial (mt-), ribosomal protein (Rps/Rpl) and cell-cycle gene. Per-cell totals are therefore about 70% of the originals, and pctMito / pctRibo from diagnoseQC() read higher than they would on the full gene set. That is fine for showing how the functions work, and wrong for drawing conclusions about the tissue.

The object was built with min.cells = 0, min.features = 0. With only ~2,000 genes kept, the seuratFrom10x() defaults would drop about 50 cells for an artefact of the subset rather than for anything wrong with them. Reading the bundled files with the defaults gives 957 cells.

Bundled Cell Ranger output

system.file("extdata", "heart_1k_v3", "outs", package = "rscprep") is a cellranger count outs/ directory holding two H5 files over the same genes:

filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5

The 1,011 called cells – what seuratFrom10x() reads.

raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5

Every barcode with at least 25 UMIs in the original run, about 20k of 6.8M – what rawMatrixFrom10x() and plotBarcodeRanks() read. Only the lowest-ranked barcodes were dropped, so the barcodes that remain keep their true ranks.

Examples

heart1k
#> An object of class Seurat 
#> 2092 features across 1011 samples within 1 assay 
#> Active assay: RNA (2092 features, 0 variable features)
#>  2 layers present: counts, data

# The same data, read from the bundled Cell Ranger output
outs <- system.file("extdata", "heart_1k_v3", "outs", package = "rscprep")
seurat_list <- seuratFrom10x(path = outs, multi = FALSE)
#> ✔ "heart_1k_v3": 957 cells, 2089 features.
#> ✔ Loaded 1 sample.
